concepts.name: Logarithms, floors and ceilings
concepts.gloss: The base-2 logarithm lg n = log2 n, the floor and ceiling functions, and the identities relating exponents, logarithms and powers of two, used to size every parameter.

concepts.name: Mathematical induction and recurrences
concepts.gloss: Proving statements for all sizes by induction and solving or bounding recursive cost recurrences such as T(n) = a T(n/b) + O(n).

concepts.name: Sorting and permutation of arrays
concepts.gloss: Sorting n items in O(n log n) steps by merging, and the notion of a permutation of positions as a bijection that rearranges an array.

concepts.name: Schoolbook multiplication and Karatsuba
concepts.gloss: Multiplying n-digit integers in O(n^2) by long multiplication, and Karatsuba's divide-and-conquer trick giving O(n^{log2 3}) with three half-size products.

concepts.name: Fast Fourier transform as an algorithm
concepts.gloss: The O(n log n) divide-and-conquer evaluation of a polynomial at the n-th roots of unity, and the idea that integer multiplication can be done through it.

concepts.name: Graphs, directed acyclic graphs and circuits
concepts.gloss: Directed graphs with vertices and edges, acyclicity, and the picture of a computation as gates joined by wires that carry values.

concepts.name: Calculus and Newton's method
aliases: reciprocal and square root by iteration
concepts.gloss: Differentiable functions, the geometric series, e^{i theta} = cos theta + i sin theta, and Newton's iteration for approximating reciprocals and square roots with quadratically shrinking error.

concepts.name: Vector norms and the triangle inequality
concepts.gloss: The size of a vector or array as its largest absolute entry, with norm of a sum bounded by the sum of norms, used to track numerical error.

concepts.name: Primes and trial division
concepts.gloss: A prime has no divisors besides 1 and itself, and primality or a nearby prime can be found deterministically by testing divisors up to the square root.

concepts.name: Rounding, rational numbers and fixed-point numbers
concepts.gloss: Representing a rational number by a scaled integer, rounding or truncating it, and bounding the error introduced by a finite number of bits.

concepts.name: Worst-case time analysis of deterministic algorithms
concepts.gloss: Bounding the maximum number of steps over all inputs of a given length, with a fixed finite constant-size table or base case handled in constant time.

concepts.name: Sets, Cartesian products and indexed arrays
concepts.gloss: The set of tuples drawn from several finite sets, used to index a multidimensional array and ordered lexicographically.

background.summary: The reader has a standard undergraduate computer science education: discrete mathematics (induction, sums, logarithms, floor and ceiling, functions and bijections, graphs and acyclic circuits), algorithms (divide and conquer, recurrences, sorting in O(n log n), grade-school multiplication and Karatsuba, Newton's method from calculus), and the basic theory of computation with Turing machines and tapes. They know complex numbers, roots of unity, polynomial arithmetic, modular arithmetic and elementary linear algebra, and have seen the FFT as an algorithm. They have not studied abstract algebra beyond modular arithmetic, number theory beyond gcd and inverses, numerical analysis of rounding errors, or any multiplication algorithm beyond the basic ones, so the wiki must explain the Fourier-transform machinery, the polynomial ring, the Harvey-van der Hoeven resampling and the linear-network constructions.
